**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make grant consumption fail when unlink loses the race**

Because `rmSync(..., { force: true })` succeeds even if another process already removed the file after this process's `statSync`, two concurrent `ratify` invocations can both observe a fresh grant and both return `true`; the second unlink is still treated as `removed = true`. That violates the single-consume cockpit grant specifically in concurrent operator/retry scenarios, allowing one gesture to authorize multiple ratifications.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow repeated ratifications to advance the sequence**

When a subjective label is contested, the operator needs to be able to re-ratify the same value to create a later ratified seq. With the ratification id keyed only by `entity_id`, `label`, `value`, and `ratified_by`, the same operator reaffirming the same value produces the old `event_id`; `appendObservationIfAbsent` then returns duplicate, so no new ratified observation is appended and the post-ratify drift remains contested indefinitely.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve contests until an operator re-ratifies**

This compares only the latest observed value with the latest ratification, so a post-ratify derive that first disagrees and then later matches the ratified value clears `contested` without any operator action. The contract above defines contested as a novel post-ratify value the operator has not adjudicated, so in that scenario the drift disappears from query/snapshot output even though no later ratification occurred.
